'''New Springville''' is a neighborhood in [[Staten Island]], one of the five [[borough (New York City)|borough]]s of [[New York City]], [[United States|USA]].

==History==
Located near the island's geographical center, the neighborhood was founded in 1680 in Karle's Neck,<ref>{{cite book|last=Smith|first=Dorothy Valentine|title=Staten Island: Gateway to New York|url=https://archive.org/details/statenislandgate0000smit|url-access=registration|year=1970|publisher=Chilton Book Company|isbn=978-0-8019-5488-7|quote = Karle's Neck: A late 1600 name for the long stretch of farm and marshland in the present New Springville area.}}</ref> 
so it was later named Karle's Neck Village.<ref>{{cite book|last=Steinmeyer|first=Henry G.|title=Holzwege|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8hcqAQAAMAAJ|year=1950|publisher=Staten Island Historical Society|page=117|quote = Springville — Sometimes called New Springville, this is the farming section of the Island. It occupies a portion of the Island known as Karle's Neck and was in 1836 called Karle's Neck Village.}}</ref>
By the early 19th century, the community included a dock (on [[Richmond Creek (Fresh Kills)|Richmond Creek]]) and several freshwater [[spring (water)|spring]]s, leading to its being renamed first Springville, then later New Springville.

New Springville remained largely rural until 1964, when the [[E. J. Korvette]] department store chain opened an outlet on the site of a former chicken farm. This was also the year the Verrazzano Narrows Bridge opened, greatly increasing population growth to the whole island. This was followed, in 1973, by the opening of the [[Staten Island Mall]] on the grounds of what had been a little-used [[airport]], which changed the character of the neighborhood completely; soon adjacent land was converted to business (mostly retail) use as well. Since then, New Springville has emerged as a commercial and administrative core, rivaling [[St. George, Staten Island|St. George]]. New Springville has also become a major public transportation hub, second in size on Staten Island only to that of the St. George ferry terminal; six city bus routes serve the area, including one going to [[Brooklyn, New York|Brooklyn]], with the terminal at the Staten Island Mall on the Marsh Avenue side ([[List of bus routes in Staten Island|the S79]]). The Yukon Bus Depot was opened in the early 1980s and can accommodate 380 buses.

The neighborhood is also known for its mafia presence. Some instances:  
* On September 11, 1989, mob-connected developer Fred Weiss was shot to death outside of his girlfriend's New Springville apartment building.  Weiss was indicted, and out of fear that he would cooperate, [[Gambino crime family]] boss [[John Gotti]] ordered Weiss's murder, and delegated the work to the [[DeCavalcante crime family]].  The hit was carried out by [[James Gallo]] and [[Vincent Palermo]].  The murder would end up resulting in multiple convictions for members of both crime families.
* In 1992, bar owner Michael Devine was shot to death in New Springville, allegedly on orders from Colombo family boss [[Alphonse Persico]], because he had been carrying on a relationship with Persico's wife while Persico was imprisoned.  
* [[2005 in organized crime|In 2005]], Gambino family capo [[Carmine Sciandra]] – accompanied by two [[Bonanno crime family|Bonanno]] gangsters – was shot non-fatally outside of his Top Tomato supermarket by a former NYPD officer whose daughter had been an employee at the supermarket.<ref>{{cite news|title=From Our Family to Yours, Bang!|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/12/14/nyregion/from-our-family-to-yours-bang.html?_r=0|work=The New York Times|date=December 14, 2005|quote=What propelled [the shooter...], the police say, was the word of his 18-year-old daughter that she had been groped by its owner, Salvatore Sciandra, while working at the store as a cashier. Whether this charge has merit remains unclear. A Sciandra family spokesman denied it, maintaining that the young woman was being nudged out of her job because receipts and cash were not adding up at her register.}}</ref>

In addition to its explosive development as a business district, New Springville also experienced massive residential growth during the latter third of the 20th century, with thousands of [[single-family home]]s being built there, along with apartment and [[Condominium (living space)|condominium]] complexes near the [[Staten Island Mall]].<ref>{{cite news|title=If You're Thinking of Living in New Springville |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/09/02/realestate/if-you-re-thining-of-living-in-new-sringville.html?pagewanted=all|work=The New York Times|date=September 2, 1984}}</ref> In recent years, a new educational complex has been under construction near these apartments and condominiums. Completed is P.S. 58 (Space Shuttle Columbia School), an elementary school, and new intermediate and high schools have been completed.

The 19th-century [[LaTourette House]] was listed on the [[National Register of Historic Places]] in 1982.<ref name="nris">{{NRISref|2010a}}</ref>

==Transportation==
Although New Springville is a major transportation hub and is well served relative to many other parts of Staten Island, it still has transportation problems. The {{NYC bus link|S44|S59|S61|S79|S91|S94|prose=y}} routes serve the area,<ref name=sibus>{{Cite NYC bus map|S}}</ref> but have no late-[[night bus|night service]].<ref name=sibus2>{{Cite NYC bus map|S2}}</ref> There are also six [[List of express bus routes in New York City#Manhattan to Staten Island|express bus]] routes: The [[SIM4 (New York City bus)|SIM4]], [[SIM4C (New York City bus)|SIM4C]], [[SIM4X (New York City bus)|SIM4X]], [[SIM8 (New York City bus)|SIM8]], [[SIM8X (New York City bus)|SIM8X]] and [[SIM31 (New York City bus)|SIM31]].<ref name=sibus/> Until 1995, New Springville had late-night bus service on the S59 route. {{As of|2010|6|28|df=us}}, however, there are no overnight buses in New Springville, the closest bus routes to New Springville during the overnight hours are the S74 bus on [[Arthur Kill Road]] at the [[Eltingville Transit Center]] to the south, and the S62 on [[Victory Boulevard (Staten Island)|Victory Boulevard]] to the north. Both of these routes are very far from the residential portion of New Springville, with the S74 and S62 being located in [[Eltingville, Staten Island|Eltingville]] and [[Bulls Head, Staten Island|Bulls Head]], respectively.<ref name=sibus/><ref name=sibus2/>

==Education==
New Springville is served by eight schools, two of which are [[expeditionary learning school]]s. One school in New Springville is a [[Charter schools in the United States|charter school]].
* two public elementary schools: P.S. 58 and P.S. 69.
* two intermediate schools: [[Rocco Laurie Intermediate School|I.S. 72]] and the Marsh Avenue School for Expeditionary Learning.
* three high schools: [[Gaynor McCown Expeditionary Learning School]], [[College of Staten Island High School for International Studies]], and the Richard H. Hungerford School.
* One Charter intermediate/high school: Richmond Preparatory Charter School.

==Demographics==
For census purposes, the New York City Department of City Planning classifies New Springville as part of a larger Neighborhood Tabulation Area called New Springville-Willowbrook-Bulls Head-Travis SI0204. This designated neighborhood had 42,871 inhabitants based on data from the [[2020 United States census|2020 United States Census]]. This was an increase of 3,561 persons (9.1%) from the 39,310 counted in [[2010 United States census|2010]]. The neighborhood had a population density of 8.5 inhabitants per acre (14,500/sq mi; 5,600/km<sup>2</sup>).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://popfactfinder.planning.nyc.gov/explorer/ntas/SI0303|title=Census Data for SI0303|date=2020|access-date=November 27, 2025|website=New York City Department of Planning|url-status=live}}</ref>

The racial makeup of the neighborhood was 59.5% (25,502) [[White Non-Hispanic|White (Non-Hispanic)]], 3.0% (1,295) [[Black Non-Hispanic|Black (Non-Hispanic)]], 19.6% (8,401) [[Asian (U.S. Census)|Asian]], and 2.6% (1,136) from two or more races. [[Hispanic (U.S. Census)|Hispanic]] or [[Latino (U.S. Census)|Latino]] of any race were 15.2% (6,537) of the population.<ref name=":0" />

According to the [[2020 United States census|2020 United States Census]], this area has many cultural communities of over 1,000 inhabitants. This include residents who identify as [[Mexican Americans|Mexican]], [[Stateside Puerto Ricans|Puerto Rican]], [[Albanian Americans|Albanian]], [[German Americans|German]], [[Irish Americans|Irish]], [[Italian Americans|Italian]], [[Polish Americans|Polish]], [[Russian Americans|Russian]], [[Egyptian Americans|Egyptian]], [[Korean Americans|Korean]], and [[Chinese Americans|Chinese]].<ref name=":0" />

71.0% of the households had at least one family present. Out of the 10,773 households, 51.0% had a married couple (20.7% with a child under 18), 4.4% had a cohabiting couple (1.4% with a child under 18), 16.8% had a single male (1.5% with a child under 18), and 27.9% had a single female (3.9% with a child under 18). 31.8% of households had children. In this neighborhood, 33.4% of non-vacant housing units are renter-occupied.<ref name=":0" />
